definition_or_difference: Walmart FY ends Jan 31 (labelled by the calendar year it ends in: FY2026 = Feb 2025-Jan 2026); Target FY ends the Saturday nearest Jan 31 (labelled by the year it begins: fiscal 2025 = ended Jan 31, 2026); Home Depot FY ends the Sunday nearest Jan 31 (labelled by start year: fiscal 2025 = ended Feb 1, 2026); Costco FY ends the Sunday nearest Aug 31 (52/53 weeks); UPS Dec 31; FedEx May 31 (FY2026 = Jun 2025-May 2026); Amazon Dec 31.
how_files_handle_it: Files carry period_end plus cal_year_approx (the calendar year in which most of the fiscal year falls: Jan-ended retailers = year before the end date; FedEx = year before; Costco and UPS = end year).

definition_or_difference: Target, Home Depot, Costco and Walmart-style 52/53 week years occasionally have 53 weeks; XBRL durations of 350-380 days are treated as annual. No adjustment for 53rd weeks.

"Distribution facilities" in Item 2 including return facilities and (from FY2014) dedicated e-commerce fulfillment centers, owned/leased and third-party operated. Count is not square footage; no DC square footage is disclosed. Retail square footage only. FY2015-2018 tables split US, Sam's, International; FY2026 merges US DCs because Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club share them.

Walmart reports dedicated e-commerce fulfillment centers separately inside the DC count (FY2015-FY2025) and states e-commerce net sales by segment in the notes. Stores also fulfil online orders (pickup, delivery from 3,500-4,300 stores), so e-commerce sales are not tied to DC counts. FY2020 e-commerce for Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club was restated upward in the FY2021 10-K (21.5 to 24.1; 3.6 to 3.8).

Revenue is total revenues incl. membership and other income (XBRL Revenues); net sales excl. membership is tagged separately. Walmart includes International (about a quarter of sales) and Sam's Club; McLane (wholesale) was sold FY2004-2010 era. SG&A tag is "operating, selling, general and administrative expenses" which includes store labor and occupancy.

Item 2 gives DC count by ownership and total DC square feet each year. From FY2022 (Jan 2023 10-K) the line is "supply chain facilities" which adds sortation centers (and from FY2023 "other facilities"), so the count jump from 48 to 55 to 58 to 66 includes a widened definition, not only new buildings.

Target reports the share of sales fulfilled by stores (about 97%) versus "other" (DCs and vendors) and the share of sales that are digitally originated (about 20%). The vast majority of digital orders are fulfilled from stores, so Target has no separate e-commerce fulfillment center count.

Revenue from FY2013-2014 included Canada (3 Canadian DCs shown separately). XBRL revenue is "Revenue" (merch sales plus other revenue) after FY2017 reclassification (credit card income moved into revenue).

Item 2 table gives square feet of "warehouses and distribution centers" (from FY2025 "distribution and fulfillment centers and warehouses") with owned/leased split, for the Primary segment. Facility counts exist only for FY2006-2016 and as lower bounds (over 400, over 500) from FY2022. The big step-ups (FY2015 Interline, FY2020-21 e-commerce and Pro buildout, FY2020 SRS in later years) reflect acquisitions and network expansion. FY2025-26 exclude SRS branch locations (over 780 / over 1,250), each of which carries its own distribution center and inventory.
FY2000-2005 10-Ks give only the HD Supply / Maintenance Warehouse distribution centers (19-21) and 13 import DCs; the retail store supply chain square footage is not disclosed until FY2006.

Online sales share of net sales is disclosed from FY2013 (3.5%) to FY2025 (15.9%); dollar amount is not stated. "Online" means ordered through websites/apps for pickup in store or delivery, so it is not equivalent to Amazon-style warehouse-fulfilled sales.

Costco has no DCs in the Amazon sense: merchandise moves through cross-dock "depots" to warehouses. Item 2 reports depot count and square feet through FY2019, then only "total square feet associated with distribution and logistics facilities" (28.0M in FY2020 versus 11.0M depots in FY2019: definition widened). Membership warehouse floor space (selling space plus storage) is reported by region and is a separate, much larger figure (138.7M FY2026).

E-commerce share of net sales is a rounded percent (3% FY2013, 7% FY2025). FY2024 adds "digitally originated" (9%, includes business delivery, travel, same-day grocery) and FY2026 reports only "digitally-enabled" (11%, includes Costco Travel). Not comparable year to year across the label change.
Revenue includes membership fees (XBRL Revenues); Costco Mexico was a 50% JV excluded from counts until consolidated in FY2011. FY2026 is the 52 weeks ended Aug 30, 2026 (10-K filed Oct 7, 2026).

UPS does not report distribution centers. Item 2 gives package operating facility count and square feet (US: over 1,000 buildings, 90M sq ft FY2025; sort hubs and delivery buildings), international package facilities (about 800, 23M sq ft) and the freight forwarding and logistics network (about 600 facilities, 50M sq ft FY2025, including 22M sq ft healthcare warehousing: this is the nearest analogue to contract warehousing). UPS stopped giving US package square feet before FY2017 in comparable form; FY2000-2016 give only logistics/non-package floor space.
No e-commerce revenue is disclosed. UPS cites business-to-consumer (B2C) volume growth qualitatively; B2C share of US volume is not in the 10-K text searched.

UPS Supply Chain Solutions was reported inside UPS; Coyote and UPS Freight were later sold (UPS Freight sold April 2021, Coyote 2023-24). Revenue and capex are company-wide including international. XBRL has no SG&A line (costs are compensation, repairs, depreciation, fuel, other); total costs and expenses is provided instead.

FedEx Ground facility counts include hubs and pickup/delivery stations (FY2002-2024), then "legacy" Ground and Express surface facilities after the 2024 consolidation into Federal Express (about 1,200 in FY2026; Item 2 says about 1,085 US operating facilities, average about 130,000 sq ft). Total square feet is not disclosed. FedEx Supply Chain (former GENCO, acquired 2015) is the contract-warehousing arm: over 150 facilities in Item 1, about 70 in Item 2 FY2026; no square feet.

FedEx headline "team members" (FY2009-2021) and "employees and contractors" (FY2001-2008) include contractors and are larger than the permanent employee figures given from FY2022 (345,000 full-time + 202,000 part-time = 547,000 in FY2022). Always check basis column.
No e-commerce revenue is disclosed. FedEx cites residential delivery coverage (99-100% of US addresses) only.
FY ends May 31, so FY2020 (ended May 2020) straddles COVID. TNT Express acquired May 2016 (large revenue and headcount step). XBRL has no SG&A line.

Item 2 gives square feet by type (fulfillment/data centers/other is one bucket), by region and by segment; no facility counts. The North America segment less physical stores and excluding AWS (data/processed/logistics_sqft_by_year.csv) is used as the network proxy and still includes Canada, Mexico, sortation centers and delivery stations. Amazon fulfillment cost (fulfillment expense line, 15.2% of sales in FY2025) includes shipping-related costs for the whole company.

Revenue includes AWS and advertising; capex includes AWS data centers and net of proceeds from sales and incentives measure is separate (not used here); PP&E includes finance leases from FY2019. Amazon capex FY2025 (131.8bn) is not a fulfillment-network figure.

Counts are not comparable across companies (Walmart counts regional DCs, return facilities and e-commerce FCs; Target counts DCs plus sortation; Costco counts depots; UPS and FedEx count package buildings). Square feet is the only common unit and only Target, Home Depot, Costco (distribution and logistics) , UPS and Amazon disclose it.
